questions.q: A database on EBS is IOPS-bound at 15,000 IOPS on a 500GB gp2 volume. Cheapest path to guaranteed high IOPS?
options: Grow the gp2 volume to 5TB (15k IOPS by size)
Migrate to gp3 with 15,000 provisioned IOPS
questions.explanation: gp3 lets you provision IOPS independent of size and is ~20% cheaper. Growing gp2 to 5TB does hit 15k IOPS but costs far more in storage.

questions.q: A queue-driven task occasionally runs 40 minutes. Lambda + SQS fails on the 15-min limit. Best fix?
options: ECS Fargate task consuming from the SQS queue
questions.explanation: Fargate has no execution time limit and integrates with SQS. Memory doesn't raise the 15-min cap; splitting may be impossible for the workload.

questions.q: A DynamoDB app has stable key-value access patterns but reads are now the bottleneck at P99. Lowest-latency AWS-native fix?
options: Add DAX in front of DynamoDB
Add ElastiCache Memcached with app rewrite
questions.explanation: DAX is an in-memory cache for DynamoDB requiring minimal code change; microsecond reads. RCU increases raise cost without fixing P99 tail; global tables are for multi-region HA.

questions.q: A reporting workload overwhelms the production RDS Postgres primary during business hours. Cheapest effective fix?
options: Add a read replica and point reporting at it
questions.explanation: Read replicas offload read-heavy reporting without touching writes on the primary. Scaling the primary fixes CPU but is costlier and still mixes workloads.
